Split row counts are bit-identical and ticker set is unchanged.

Immaterial to the comparison.

signal_rule_applied: CLAUDE.md compound rule: AUC>0.55 => discriminating. eval AUC 0.56->0.59 (both >0.55); test AUC 0.44->0.55. Weighted R-precision lift well above 1.5x post-fix on both segments => real top-tail signal, strengthened by the fix.
headline: The sample-uniqueness fix did NOT overturn the signal verdict (this cell discriminates in both runs) but it DID change two conclusions: (1) calibration flipped from native (z=0.85) to isotonic (z=-4.81) — post-fix raw probabilities are under-confident and need the isotonic layer; (2) top-tail ranking strengthened — eval weighted R-precision 0.171->0.214 and test 0.031->0.094 (test flipped from below-base-rate to clear signal), and best_iteration moved 0->1. Panel size was CONSTANT (same 46 tickers, identical 36800/18400/9200/2300 split rows); the #167 back-extend did not confound.
